_about: The known limits of a detection rule, by rule id or by family (class:<rule class>), each from a measurement or an audit with its source. scripts/rule_provenance.py adds them to the provenance of each rule; tests/test_rule_provenance.py checks that every key names a rule. Ids and words only, never a value.
us-bank: Its label must stand before the number on the same line, within 60 characters: a table row whose label is the header line above is missed (docs/BENCHMARKS.md, Benchmark V1, 73 of 9,051 Nemotron accounts).
It also takes bank routing codes and policy numbers after an account word (V3 audit, Gretel dev: 4 of 40 sampled false positives were bank codes).
us-ssn: A policy or claim number in the SSN shape is taken (V3 audit, Nemotron dev: 1 of 40).
Most of its false positives on Nemotron are real SSNs the dataset did not label (V3 audit: 38 of 40).
FP audit 2026-10-20, Nemotron dev, 12 by order: 10 are real SSNs after an SSN word without a label; 1 is a medical record number.
us-passport: A nine-digit reference in an EDI or SWIFT message or a claim number is taken (V3 audit, Gretel and Nemotron dev).
FP audit 2026-10-20, Gretel dev, 12 by order: 11 are fields of SWIFT MT, EDIFACT, X12 or XBRL messages, 1 unclear.
us-license: Reference numbers of the same shape are taken: recall and campaign numbers, transmission dates, CAS numbers, hazard codes (V3 audit, Gretel and Nemotron dev).
FP audit 2026-10-20, Gretel dev, 12 by order: 7 are GHS hazard codes, EDI fields, an HL7 trigger event or an FpML scheme; 3 are company or property numbers.
medical-license: The DEA pattern has no word boundary; a hit is widened to its whole token after the validator (0.6.43). A DEA-shaped part of an unrelated token that passes the check digit is masked whole too.
de-plz: A five-digit number after a postcode label that is no postcode (an application number) is taken (V3 audit, Gretel dev).
Alone it masks only the postcode of a German address; the street and the city stay in the clear unless an address rule takes the line (Gretel dev, 113 addresses found in part on 2026-10-20).
address-after-label: Its value runs to the end of the sentence when no stop follows, so it can be wider than the address (2026-10-20, a label followed by a street and running text).
csv-personal-column: A row counts only with a person in it (a name of two words, a birth date or an id): a list of depots or of cities stays text on purpose, and so does a row with a first name alone.
A name with an apostrophe (O'Brien) fails the name check, and with it its row (2026-10-20).
md-table-personal-column: The same person check as the CSV rule, without the birth date as a person.
sql-insert-personal-column: A tuple without its end and a statement without a column list name no cell.
html-table-personal-column: A cell with two text runs or a nested table, and a table without <th> in its first row, name no cell.
json-personal-field: An object inside an array under a person's key is no part of the person's record (one level of nesting, no arrays).
xml-personal-field: Two levels of nesting below the element that names the person are not joined; an element with text and child elements both is no record.
ip: It takes values inside EDIFACT segments (FP audit 2026-10-20, Gretel dev: all 16 false positives are such segments).
phone: It takes numbers inside EDI and SWIFT segments (FP audit 2026-10-20, Gretel dev, 12 by order: 4), and the phone and fax lines of companies (6), which are no person's.
ds-keyword-colon: It takes a value after labels that are no secret label: an encryption setting after Verschlüsselung, an amount after passivo or passifs (FP audit 2026-10-20, Gretel dev, 12 by order: 4).
